summary: Govind Chandra Pande worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya (~1943–1947). His appointments included posts at the University of Allahabad, University of Rajasthan, Allahabad Museum, and Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye worked in Indology and sociology. He studied at Bahauddin College, Elphinstone College, and the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon. He headed Mumbai University's Department of Sociology (1924–1959).

Govind Swamirao Gai was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India (attested 1958–1966) and Chief Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976).

Govind Vinayak Devasthali worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944). He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts and RYK Science College (attested 1944) and Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).
Govind Vishnu Kathavate was an Indologist. He succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and held the Sanskrit chair at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist. He served as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).

Grace S. Fong is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia. She was a professor at Smith College (~1985–1989) and became associate professor and chair of East Asian Studies at McGill University (~1989).

Graeme MacQueen worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and served as a lecturer at McMaster University from circa 1978 to 2003.

Grafton Elliot Smith was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Sydney Medical School, the University of Sydney, and St John's College, and later held a post at University College London from circa 1919 to 1937.

Graham E. Clarke worked in Tibetology and related fields. He held appointments at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was attested as a Senior Member in 1998.
Graham Lock is a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Parkes works in philosophy and Japanology. After completing his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~1974–1978), he served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1990–2007) and Professor of Philosophy at University College Cork (~2008–2013).

Graham Priest works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge, St John's College, and the London School of Economics under John Lane Bell. His posts include positions at the University of Melbourne and the Graduate Center, CUNY.

Graves Chamney Haughton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Fort William College. He served as Professor of Hindú Literature, and the History of Asia at East India Company College (1819–1827) and secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Gray Tuttle works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University in 2002 under Leonard van der Kuijp, William C. Kirby, and Philip A. Kuhn. He was an associate professor at Columbia University (attested 2008–2015).

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli was an Italian scholar of linguistics and Indology. He founded the *Archivio glottologico italiano* in 1873 and served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.
Greg Bailey is an Indologist who studied under Madeleine Biardeau and doctoral supervisor J. Durham. He held academic posts, including professor, at La Trobe University (attested 1994, 2004).

Gregor Ahn works in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Copenhagen and Bonn under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. He taught at Münster and Tartu before becoming Professor of Comparative Religion at Heidelberg University in 1996.

Gregory Forgues works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where he was supervised by Helmut Tauscher and Birgit Kellner, and studied with several traditional teachers.

Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa, UC Santa Barbara, and Oxford (Wolfson College), completing doctoral work under Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson, and also studied under Harunaga Isaacson.
